paper_title: Non-adaptive vs Adaptive Queries in the Dense Graph Testing Model
authors: Oded Goldreich (Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel), Avi Wigderson (Institute for Advanced Study, USA)
statement: 1) Our separation results assert the mere existence of graph properties that exhibit gaps in their testing complexity. This raises the question of whether such gaps can be proved for properties that are efficiently recognizable. Furthermore, one may seek efficient testers for such properties; that is, testers whose time complexity is closely related to their query complexity. For Theorems 1.2–1.4 and 1.6–1.7, this challenge was meet in a subsequent work [9] (see [9, Cor. 1.9] and a subsequent comment), but it remains open for Theorem 1.5.
context: open problems. In particular: 1) Our separation results assert the mere existence of graph properties that exhibit gaps in their testing complexity. This raises the question of whether such gaps can be proved for properties that are efficiently recognizable. Furthermore, one may seek efficient testers for such properties; that is, testers whose time complexity is closely related to their query complexity. For Theorems 1.2–1.4 and 1.6–1.7, this challenge was meet in a subsequent work [9] (see [9, Cor. 1.9] and a subsequent comment), but it remains open for Theorem 1.5. Our results rely on graphs that are both robustly selfordered and have local self-ordering procedures. As we show, random graphs happen to satisfy these two features, but one may ask whether one feature implies the other. This question is the focus of [9], where it is considered both for the dense graph model (as here) and for the bounded-degree graph model.
